item.text: I’m looking for the next refactor that reduces actual technical debt, not just rearranges names. The main issue now is that the code still converts the same selection into different shapes ad hoc, so I’m going to consolidate that behind one result model and then rerun the tests.

I’m replacing the parallel “count API” and “pair API” plumbing with one selection result object so the schedule only computes one thing internally. Then I’ll have the legacy methods delegate to that result and keep the tests focused on behavior.
The result model is in place. I’m recompiling and rerunning now to confirm the new wrapper didn’t change the behavior or introduce copying mistakes.

Refactored [ActivitySelection.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:1) around a single `SelectionResult` model. The count API and selected-activities API now both delegate to `buildSelectionResult(...)`, so the schedule computes one coherent result instead of exposing parallel conversions from different paths.

I also extended [ActivitySelectionTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelectionTest.java:1) to validate the new result object alongside the existing count and activity-pair assertions, which gives better coverage for the refactor surface.
